# Reasoning about Intent for Ambiguous Requests

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#intentrl)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.10453v4) · arXiv:2511.10453v4, 8 August 2026; PDF identifies publication at COLM 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 37 pages: sections 1–6, references and Appendices A–K, including all prompts, reward equations, ablations, human-study details and complete example outputs; reasoning-length figure visually inspected.

## Research question

Models often commit to one plausible interpretation or produce opaque alternatives, even when a question admits several valid answers.

## Method

IntentRL applies DAPO to generate up to five interpretation–answer pairs in one response. Ambiguous training examples receive answer-set recall reward; unambiguous examples receive precision reward. Three-to-one oversampling of ambiguous cases counteracts training collapse toward one answer.

## Evaluation

The main Qwen3-4B model is tested on Abg-CoQA and AMBROSIA, with AMBROSIA-to-AmbiQT transfer, other model families, reward/data-format ablations and a simulated clarification pipeline. Human raters assess interpretation–answer compatibility on 30 ambiguous examples per main dataset.

## What the results support

On AMBROSIA, reported full coverage rises from 58.8% for SFT to 74.1%; on AmbiQT it reaches 49.1%. Balancing is important, while answer-only RL remains competitive. SQL precision stays imperfect, and conversational QA frequently over-generates alternatives.

## Limits and qualifications

Human alignment judgments explicitly allow incorrect answers and do not establish truth, user preference or safer decisions. The five-answer limit excludes large interpretation spaces; execution matching remains instance-dependent. Clarification comparisons use simulated users and untrained clarification stages. One generation does not imply lower token cost, and precision is not directly rewarded on ambiguous examples.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Offers a trainable coverage-versus-restraint baseline and structured alternatives for clarification interfaces, with a clear distinction between answer coverage, explanation alignment and actual user-intent resolution.

| All gains arise from explicit interpretation output. | Answer-only IntentRL is competitive; removing ambiguity oversampling sharply reduces coverage. | Tables 9, 14; Appendices G, H.1 | Attribute gains to training objective and sampling, not format alone. |
